author: GitHub
description:
"Building in the open" usually means one thing: code on GitHub. As engineers, the Home Assistant team will tell you that's the easy part, the hard work starts long before code with UX, design, architecture, and roadmaps. In this GitHub Universe 2026 session, Franck Nijhof, Lead of Home Assistant, reveals how the Open Home Foundation coordinates over 20,000 contributors across hundreds of repositories. Learn how GitHub Discussions, Issues, and Projects power a living public roadmap where anyone can shape features before a line of code is written. 

Speakers: 
Franck Nijhof, Lead of Home Assistant, Open Home Foundation

Watch more videos from GitHub Universe 2026: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AArI948SDz8&list=PLENrlACZ7mnU

— CHAPTERS —

00:00 The gap between code and direction
01:59 Introducing Home Assistant and Open decision-making
02:54 Round 1: encrypted backups decision
04:02 Round 2: redesigning the login screen
05:39 Opening the public roadmap on GitHub
06:44 From feature req
title: Code is the easy part: building Home Assistant in the open

author: GitHub
description:
You can read the original source code that sent Apollo 11 to the Moon right on GitHub. Led by Margaret Hamilton and the MIT team, the Apollo Guidance Computer software spanned around 145,000 lines of assembly code and is filled with programmer comments from over 50 years ago—including an ignition routine called "Burn Baby Burn." Discover how its priority scheduling recovered from critical 1201 and 1202 overload alarms during the lunar descent. Explore the complete repository at https://github.com/chrislgarry/apollo-11

#GitHub #OpenSource #Apollo11
